name: Maheshwari saree
subcategory: Geographical Indication craft of Madhya Pradesh
summary: Maheshwari saree is a traditional textile woven in the town of Maheshwar in Madhya Pradesh, India.
description:
Maheshwari saree is a traditional textile woven in the town of Maheshwar in Madhya Pradesh, India. Made using a combination of cotton and silk yarn, the fabric is used to produce saris, salwar suits, dupattas, and home furnishings.

The craft received Geographical Indication (GI) status in 2010 to safeguard its production methods and regional identity.
culturalContext: Registered as a Geographical Indication of India (handicraft, Madhya Pradesh; registration 2012–13), which protects the name for products made in its place of origin by traditional methods.

visualDNA.Overview: Maheshwari sarees are characterized by a lightweight body, using fine cotton thread in the weft and silk in the warp to provide structure and a slight sheen.
visualDNA.Design and motifs: The motifs used on the borders and loose ends (pallu) are primarily geometric, often influenced by the architectural carvings, fort walls, and ghats along the Narmada River.
visualDNA.Distinctive features: Reversible border: Traditional Maheshwari saris frequently feature a reversible border known locally as bugdi, allowing the sari to be worn from either side. Five-stripe pallu: The pallu typically incorporates five horizontal stripes, alternating between two light bands and three colored bands.

recipe.technique: The production process is carried out on pit looms and frame looms across weaving centers in Maheshwar.
